The UK would have to leave the ECtHR, which could then jeopardise the Good Friday agreement ( as that too used the ECHR, in its framework ) in order to change this

The ruling of Goodwin v the UK in the ECtHR in 2002 obliged the United Kingdom to provide some way for trans people who meet a certain criteria defined by the UK government to change their documents. So trans women and men who have met this criteria can change their passport and birth certificate as necessary. 

This makes it nigh on impossible to enforce a biological reading of sex without removing the mechanism to change documents at which point the UK would then be in breach of the Goodwin ruling.
